_comment: Source of truth for /grants/. 'deadlines' is an array of upcoming ISO dates; leave empty for rolling deadlines (the entry will appear under 'Rolling & annually recurring').

grants.name: NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The 2027 competition deadlines were 19 to 23 October 2026, depending on field. Check the funder's site for the next competition.
grants.amount: USD 37,000/yr stipend + USD 16,000/yr cost of education allowance
grants.description: Three-year fellowship for early-career graduate students in NSF-supported STEM disciplines, including computer & information sciences.

grants.name: Goldwater Scholarship
grants.deadlineNote: Campus deadlines run earlier; check your institutional rep.
grants.amount: Up to USD 7,500/yr
grants.description: Undergraduate award for U.S. sophomores and juniors intending research careers in natural sciences, engineering, and mathematics.

grants.name: Knight-Hennessy Scholars
grants.deadlineNote: The application for the 2027 cohort closed on 6 October 2026. Knight-Hennessy states the application for the 2028 cohort will open in June 2027.
grants.amount: Full tuition + stipend
grants.description: Graduate scholarship at Stanford open globally; supports doctoral and masters study across the sciences and beyond.

grants.name: Rhodes Scholarship
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for 2027 entry are closed. Applications reopen in 2027 for entry to Oxford in 2028; deadlines vary by constituency.
grants.amount: Full tuition + stipend
grants.description: Postgraduate scholarship for study at the University of Oxford; multiple constituencies, including India.

grants.name: HFSP Postdoctoral Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call. For the 2027 cycle the LOI closed 12 May 2026 and invited full proposals closed 24 September 2026. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: Approx. USD 55,000/yr + allowances
grants.description: Postdoctoral fellowships for life-science research with an international move; cross-disciplinary track open to physicists, chemists, computer scientists, and engineers entering life sciences.

grants.name: EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: Applications accepted year-round with two cutoffs a year; next hard deadline 22 January 2027, 14:00 CET.
grants.amount: Salary + family/travel allowances
grants.description: Two-year postdoctoral fellowships for molecular life sciences research in EMBC member states and partner countries.

grants.name: Marie Skłodowska-Curie Postdoctoral Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call with European and Global Fellowship streams. The 2026 call closed 9 September 2026. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: Salary + mobility/family allowance
grants.description: Mobility fellowships supporting postdoctoral researchers in any discipline, hosted in or moving to Europe.

grants.name: Schmidt Science Fellows
grants.funder: Schmidt Sciences (in partnership with Rhodes Trust)
grants.deadlineNote: Nominations come from partner universities; check internal deadlines.
grants.amount: USD 110,000/yr stipend
grants.description: Postdoctoral fellowship for early-career scientists pivoting into a new discipline to tackle interdisciplinary problems.

grants.name: Damon Runyon Postdoctoral Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The 2026 deadline was 14 August 2026. Check the funder's site for the 2027 date.
grants.amount: USD 70,000-76,000/yr (graduated)
grants.description: Four-year fellowship for theoretical and experimental approaches in cancer research, broadly defined.

grants.name: Sloan Research Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: Nomination by department head. Nominations for the 2027 fellowships ran 15 July to 15 September 2026; the next cycle has not been announced.
grants.description: Two-year fellowship for outstanding early-career faculty in seven scientific fields, including computer science and mathematics.

grants.name: Packard Fellowships for Science and Engineering
grants.deadlineNote: Annual; only 50 invited universities may nominate. In the 2026 cycle institutional nominations were due 15 March and applications 20 April. The 2027 dates are not yet posted.
grants.amount: USD 875,000 over 5 years
grants.description: Unrestricted five-year award supporting early-career faculty in the natural and physical sciences and engineering.

grants.name: NSF CAREER Award
grants.deadlineNote: Annual deadline on the fourth Wednesday in July, 5 p.m. submitter's local time (NSF 22-586).
grants.description: Foundation-wide award for early-career faculty integrating research and education.

grants.name: ERC Starting Grant
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The ERC-2027 Starting Grant call closed 14 October 2026. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: Up to EUR 1.5 million
grants.description: European frontier-research grant for promising early-career investigators, open across all disciplines.

grants.name: ANRF Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call announced on the ANRF portal. ANRF's 2026 calendar, as reported by Careers360, lists a window of 2 November to 2 December 2026; confirm on the portal.
grants.amount: Up to INR 60 lakh plus overheads over three years
grants.description: Five-year early-career grant for researchers in Indian institutions across the sciences.

grants.name: Royal Society University Research Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: The 2027 round closed on 9 September 2026, with decisions by 31 May 2027. The Royal Society expects the 2028 round to open in July 2027 and close by the end of September 2027.
grants.amount: Salary contribution + research expenses
grants.description: Long fellowship for outstanding early-career scientists to establish independent research groups at UK or Republic of Ireland host institutions.

grants.name: HHMI Investigator Program
grants.deadlineNote: The next Investigator competition opens 28 September 2027 and closes 7 March 2028, for faculty with at least seven years as lab head.
grants.amount: Full salary + lab + benefits
grants.description: Long-term investment in mid-career biomedical scientists; HHMI employs the investigator and supports the lab.

grants.name: DIA Research Translation Accelerator
grants.funder: Centre for Cellular and Molecular Platforms (C-CAMP)
grants.deadlineNote: The call closed 30 June 2026. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.description: Accelerator for proof-of-concept innovations (TRL-3) in healthcare, agriculture, and environment, transforming them into scalable industry solutions.

grants.name: ANRF MAHA Water Programme
grants.funder: Anusandhan National Research Foundation & Ministry of Jal Shakti
grants.deadlineNote: Consortium-mode proposals; calls are announced on the ANRF portal. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: Up to ₹20 crore
grants.description: Mission-driven research on India's water challenges - sustainable management, drinking-water access, climate resilience, and water quality.

grants.name: Collaborative Scientific Research Programme (CSRP)
grants.funder: Indo-French Centre for the Promotion of Advanced Research (CEFIPRA)
grants.deadlineNote: The current call is closed. CEFIPRA runs two calls a year (a Thematic Call and a General Call); check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: Up to €220,000 (combined)
grants.description: Indo-French collaborative research in mathematics, physics, chemistry, life sciences, materials science, environmental sciences, and biotechnology.

grants.name: Research Scholars Program - HIV / Viral Hepatitis
grants.deadlineNote: Applications are closed; the funder says the next call will open soon. Check the funder's site.
grants.description: Supports independent early-career investigators in HIV and viral hepatitis research aligned with sustainable development goals.

grants.name: Global Health Research - Tackling AMR in Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia
grants.funder: National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR)
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026 call closed on 8 July 2026. It is part of the NIHR Global Health Research Themed Programme, which runs yearly with a new theme each year.
grants.amount: £0.5M – £5M (banded)
grants.description: Bacterial and fungal AMR research on WHO priority lists, addressing real-world gaps in stewardship, infection prevention, and AMR-related health outcomes.

grants.name: Rowland Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026 deadline (1 August) has passed. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: USD 89,999/yr + Harvard benefits
grants.description: Establishes independent experimental research programmes in any science or engineering field at Harvard's Rowland Institute, Cambridge, MA.

grants.name: U.S.–India TRUST Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026-27 cycle closed 30 June 2026. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: USD 1,650/mo (postdoc) or USD 3,650/mo (Visiting Faculty)
grants.description: U.S.-based researchers spend a year at IIT Madras, IISc, or MAHE working on AI, quantum computing, semiconductors, biotechnology, defence, energy, or space.

grants.name: OpenAI Economic Research Exchange
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026 RFP closed on 5 July 2026 and a research cohort was announced in August 2026. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: USD 25,000 PI grant + USD 7,500/mo RA stipend
grants.description: Funds empirical research on the economic impacts of AI using privacy-preserving analysis of OpenAI product and usage data - labour markets, education, household welfare, market structure, knowledge production.

grants.name: MultiObs Postdoctoral Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026 call for eight FAPESP postdoctoral fellowships closed on 20 July 2026. No postdoctoral call is currently listed; check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: FAPESP rates + contingency fund
grants.description: Postdoc positions at UNICAMP across Living Lab, Data Infrastructure, Diversity & Funding Dynamics, Technology & Innovation, and STI Diplomacy workplans.

grants.name: Sydney Brenner Research Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The 2026 deadline was 15 October 2026 for the following academic year. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: Up to USD 5,000
grants.description: Supports research in the history of the life sciences using CSHL's Carnegie Library collections and archival staff.

grants.name: Hubert H. Humphrey Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: The 2027-2028 cycle closed 9 July 2026. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.description: Non-degree academic + professional placement for mid-career leaders in policy fields including natural-resources, public-health, and technology policy.

grants.name: NIF Book Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 15 November 2026. Indian citizens; non-fiction on contemporary India.
grants.description: Supports research and writing of original non-fiction books on contemporary India; stipend, editorial support, and publication with leading houses.

grants.name: Hanse-Wissenschaftskolleg Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: Scientific fellowship applications (Junior and Regular tracks, one form) open 1 March and close 15 July 2027 at midnight CEST.
grants.description: Residential fellowship at HWK Delmenhorst; science streams include Brain & Mind, Earth, and Technology & Science.

grants.name: Leakey Foundation Research Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Two cycles a year: 10 January (spring, decisions mid-May) and 15 July (fall). Open to PhD candidates (ABD) and post-PhD researchers.
grants.description: Funds research on human origins - paleoanthropology (Miocene/Pliocene/Pleistocene), primate evolution and behaviour, and modern hunter-gatherer groups.
grants.amount: Up to USD 20,000 (PhD candidates) or USD 30,000 (post-PhD)

grants.name: LOTUS Programme - India–Japan Joint Research
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call; FY2026 cycle closed 9 Jun 2026. Watch JST for FY2027 announcement.
grants.description: Indian Master's, PhD, and postdoctoral researchers for joint research stays in Japan across AI/robotics, biotechnology, energy, materials, quantum, semiconductors, and networks/telecom.

grants.name: Tata Transformation Prize
grants.funder: Tata Group & New York Academy of Sciences
grants.deadlineNote: Annual prize; 2026 cycle closed 29 May. Watch NYAS for the 2027 call.
grants.description: Recognises India-based scientists and engineers developing transformational technologies in food security, sustainability, or healthcare.
grants.amount: INR 2 crore per winner, one winner in each of three categories (food security, sustainability, healthcare)

grants.name: Advanced Research Grant (ARG)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call. ANRF's 2026 calendar had pre-proposals in April to May and full proposals from 15 September to 15 October 2026; both stages have closed. Check the ANRF portal for the next call.
grants.amount: Up to INR 5 crore
grants.description: Restructured successor to the SERB Core Research Grant (CRG). Supports high-impact fundamental (TRL 1-3) and applied (TRL 1-6) research in frontier areas of science and engineering at academic institutions, national labs, and DSIR-SIRO recognised organisations.

grants.name: ARG-MATRICS (Mathematical Research Impact-Centric Support)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call under the ARG umbrella; the 2026 window has closed. Check the ANRF portal for the next call.
grants.amount: INR 5 lakh/year + overheads (incl. up to INR 5 lakh international travel)
grants.description: Supports active researchers in mathematical sciences, theoretical sciences (all areas of science and engineering other than mathematical), and quantitative analytical work. Streamlined fixed-grant scheme for established mathematicians and theoretical scientists.

grants.name: J. C. Bose Grant (JBG)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual nominations; the 2026 window closed 10 February 2026. Check the ANRF portal for the next call.
grants.amount: INR 25 lakh/year research grant plus INR 1 lakh/year overheads, for five years
grants.description: Recognises active senior scientists and engineers in India (age 45-65) for outstanding performance and contributions. By nomination from Heads of Institutions/Universities or Presidents of Science Academies. Indian nationals or OCIs in senior positions at Indian institutions.

grants.name: Ramanujan Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: Always open. Nominations are accepted throughout the year and selections are announced twice a year.
grants.amount: INR 1.35 lakh/month fellowship + research grant
grants.description: For brilliant Indian/Indian-origin scientists and engineers (under age 40) currently abroad to take up scientific research positions in India. Year-round nominations through institutions; one of the ANRF schemes that remains open year-round.

grants.name: POWER Fellowship (Promoting Opportunities For Women in Exploratory Research)
grants.deadlineNote: Always open. Nominations accepted throughout the year via online portal; no last date. Selection made twice a year.
grants.amount: INR 15,000/month in addition to salary plus INR 10 lakh/year research grant, for three years
grants.description: Mitigates gender disparity in S&T research funding. Recognises and supports outstanding women scientists in active research in Indian academic institutions and R&D labs. One of the two ANRF schemes that remain open year-round.

grants.name: POWER Research Grant
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling/year-round applications via the ANRF portal; selections made on Program Advisory Committee recommendations. Level I (premier institutions) up to INR 60 lakh; Level II (state universities/private colleges) up to INR 30 lakh.
grants.amount: Level I up to INR 60 lakh; Level II up to INR 30 lakh
grants.description: Two-tier research grant for women scientists (Level I and Level II based on career stage). Supports independent research projects in science and engineering at Indian academic institutions and R&D labs.

grants.name: National Post Doctoral Fellowship (N-PDF)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call; the 2026 window closed 17 February 2026. Calls are announced on the ANRF portal and usually stay open for about one month.
grants.amount: INR 80,000/month (PhD awarded); INR 50,000/month (thesis submitted) + research grant
grants.description: Supports early-career researchers with a PhD to carry out independent postdoctoral research in Indian institutions. Upper age 35 (relaxations apply).

grants.name: International Travel Support (ITS)
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling, event-tied: applications accepted in a 60-90 day window before event start date. Not eligible if availed in past 3 years.
grants.amount: Economy airfare, airport tax, visa fees; young scientists also get registration up to INR 50,000
grants.description: Financial assistance for Indian researchers to present research at international scientific events (conferences, seminars, workshops) abroad, and for young scientists (under 35) to attend training programmes and schools.

grants.name: Visiting Advanced Joint Research (VAJRA) Faculty Scheme
grants.deadlineNote: Applications are accepted year-round. The committee meets in January and July, and results are announced in April and September.
grants.amount: USD 15,000 first month + USD 10,000 each subsequent month (pro-rata)
grants.description: Adjunct/visiting faculty assignments for overseas scientists (incl. NRI/PIO/OCI) to undertake collaborative research at Indian public-funded academic and research institutions.

grants.name: KARYASHALA - High-End Workshop (Accelerate Vigyan)
grants.deadlineNote: Applications invited twice a year: May (for winter workshops Nov-Jan) and November (for summer workshops May-Jul) via the Accelerate Vigyan portal.
grants.amount: Workshop organisation support
grants.description: Supports high-end hands-on training workshops at IITs, IISc, IISERs, NITs, CSIR/ICAR/ICMR labs for PG and PhD students from universities, colleges, and newly established institutes. Workshop hosts apply; students apply to selected workshops.

grants.name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence (TARE)
grants.deadlineNote: Call-based; notified periodically via ANRF/SERB websites. No active 2026 call confirmed on the official page.
grants.amount: INR 60,000/year fellowship (in addition to regular salary) + INR 5 lakh/yr research grant (split 50/50 between host and parent institutions) + overheads
grants.description: Facilitates mobility of faculty in State Universities, colleges, and private academic institutions to carry out research at established public-funded institutions (IITs, IISc, IISERs, NITs, CSIR/ICAR/ICMR labs, Central Universities).

grants.name: MAHA Drones - Components and Sub-Assemblies R&I Program
grants.deadlineNote: Stage 1 pre-proposal call: 27 April - 26 May 2026 (closed). Stage 2 to follow for shortlisted consortia.
grants.amount: Up to INR 50 Crore per consortium over 3 years
grants.description: Joint with ICMR and Ministry of Earth Sciences. Strengthens India's drone ecosystem by promoting indigenous development of critical components (motors, ESCs, Li-ion cells, GNSS, secure radios, EO/IR cameras, LiDAR, SAR payloads, sensors) and post-quantum cryptography.

grants.name: MAHA AI for Science and Engineering (AI-SE)
grants.deadlineNote: Mission launched in 2026 in collaboration with MeitY and scientific departments. Check ANRF portal for active CFPs.
grants.amount: Up to INR 30 Crore for 3-year projects (up to INR 50 Crore in exceptional cases); GPU usage capped at 70% of budget via MeitY infrastructure
grants.description: Flagship MAHA initiative supporting AI-driven research across science and engineering, in collaboration with MeitY, MoES, DBT, and DRDO. Covers foundation models for scientific discovery and AI applications in physical and life sciences.

grants.name: Ramalingaswami Re-entry Fellowship
grants.funder: Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: No call is open on DBT's call-for-proposals page. Check that page for the next round.
grants.amount: Fellowship of INR 1.35 lakh/month + INR 8.5 lakh/yr research grant + HRA
grants.duration: 3 years (extendable by up to 2 more years after performance appraisal)
grants.description: Re-entry fellowship for Indian nationals working abroad in biotechnology and life sciences who wish to return and take up scientific research in India.

grants.name: BioCARe - Biotechnology Career Advancement and Re-orientation for Women Researchers (2026-27)
grants.funder: Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026-27 call is no longer listed as open. Check DBT's call-for-proposals page for the next round.
grants.amount: Up to INR 60 lakh (Cat-I) or INR 40 lakh (Cat-II) including fellowship
grants.description: First extramural research grant for women scientists in biotechnology and allied areas to advance or re-establish research careers. Category I: PhD in Biotechnology / Life Sciences / allied or interdisciplinary areas, or MD / MDS / M.V.Sc. Category II: M.Tech in Biotechnology / allied areas, M.Pharma, or equivalent.

grants.name: DBT/Wellcome Trust India Alliance Fellowships (Early Career / Intermediate / Senior)
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026 Senior, Intermediate and Clinical and Public Health calls closed between March and April 2026. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: Up to INR 3.6 Cr (ECF) / INR 4.5 Cr (IF) / Senior tier research funds + salary support
grants.description: Flagship biomedical fellowships supporting independent researchers in India across basic, clinical, public health and veterinary sciences; the principal non-government biomedical fellowship in India.

grants.name: INSPIRE Faculty Fellowship
grants.funder: Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call through the INSPIRE portal. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: INR 1.25 lakh/month consolidated + INR 7 lakh/yr research grant
grants.description: Faculty-level fellowship for young researchers (<32 years at award) with PhD in basic/applied sciences, engineering, medicine, agriculture, providing assured opportunity to do independent research at any recognised Indian institution.

grants.name: Women Scientist Scheme-B (WOS-B)
grants.funder: Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling submissions through online-wosa portal under WISE-KIRAN.
grants.amount: Fellowship + project grant (varies by level/PhD/MTech)
grants.description: Supports women scientists with a career break to take up S&T-based projects addressing societal problems. Part of the WISE-KIRAN umbrella (which also includes WISE-PDF, WISE-PHD, and the separate WIDUSHI scheme for senior women scientists in interdisciplinary research).

grants.name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant (BIG)
grants.funder: Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC), DBT
grants.deadlineNote: Two calls per year; 25th call announced in early 2026, calls typically open ~45 days.
grants.amount: Up to INR 50 lakh grant-in-aid
grants.description: Flagship early-stage biotech startup grant for scientist entrepreneurs and incubatee companies to translate ideas to proof of concept.

grants.name: ICMR ANVESHAN Extramural Grants (Small / Intermediate / Follow-on)
grants.deadlineNote: No ANVESHAN or NISCHAYAK call is open; results of the 2026 round are posted on ICMR's call page. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: ANVESHAN (Small) up to INR 2 crore over up to 3 years; NISCHAYAK (Intermediate) INR 2-8 crore over up to 4 years; follow-on grants in the same ranges
grants.description: Investigator-initiated biomedical research grants across the ICMR ANVESHAN extramural family covering biomedical, clinical, public health and translational research.

grants.name: ISRO RESPOND - Sponsored Research Programme
grants.funder: Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), Department of Space
grants.deadlineNote: RESPOND Basket 2025 currently referenced on ISRO portal; cycles per ISRO centre (VSSC, SAC, URSC, NRSC, LPSC, IPRC, PRL, IIRS, NESAC, ISTRAC, HSFC). Check ISRO site for 2026 updates.
grants.amount: Project-based (varies by problem statement)
grants.description: Mission-oriented academic R&D in space technology, space science and space applications via collaboration with Indian universities and research institutes.

grants.name: DAE-BRNS Research Projects
grants.funder: Board of Research in Nuclear Sciences (BRNS), Department of Atomic Energy
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling/year-round submission via BRNS portal across thrust areas of physical, chemical, biological, engineering and material sciences.
grants.amount: Project-based; equipment, manpower and contingency support
grants.description: Extramural research grants for university/institute scientists in nuclear and allied sciences, engineering and technology of relevance to DAE.

grants.name: National Agricultural Science Fund (NASF)
grants.deadlineNote: Periodic calls for research pre-proposals via NASF portal.
grants.amount: Project-based; consortium grants
grants.description: Supports basic, strategic and frontier-application research in agriculture (genomics, climate-resilient agriculture, nanotechnology, sensors, plant/animal sciences) through consortium-mode projects.

grants.name: MNRE Research, Development & Demonstration (RD&D) Programme
grants.funder: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: MNRE posts specific calls for proposals on its R&D portal. The R&D programme was approved for continuation for 2026-27 to 2030-31; check the funder's site for open calls.
grants.amount: Up to 100% support for govt/non-profit; 50-70% for industry
grants.description: Funds R&D and demonstration projects in renewable energy technologies; also supports the National Renewable Energy Science Fellowship (NRESF) at INR 1.2 lakh/month plus research grant.

grants.name: PRITHVI - Earth Sciences Research Programme (ACROSS/O-SMART/PACER/SAGE)
grants.funder: Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: PRITHVI Vigyan (PRITHVI) is the MoES overarching scheme (2021-2026) merging ACROSS, O-SMART, PACER, SAGE, and REACHOUT; calls under sub-schemes announced periodically. Scheme cycle ends 2026; renewal pending.
grants.amount: Rs 4,797 crore allocation (2021-26) across atmosphere, ocean, polar, seismology, and REACHOUT sub-schemes
grants.description: PRITHVI Vigyan umbrella scheme of MoES funding extramural and collaborative research across five sub-schemes: ACROSS (atmosphere/climate), O-SMART (ocean), PACER (polar/cryosphere), SAGE (seismology/geosciences), and REACHOUT (research/training/outreach).

grants.name: Google Academic Research Awards
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026 call ran 26 June to 7 August 2026, with decisions expected 30 October 2026. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: Cash awards + Google Cloud credits
grants.description: Unrestricted gifts and Google Cloud credits to faculty (especially early-career) for foundational and applied research in computing and technology. Consolidates the former Research Scholar Program and Faculty Research Awards.

grants.name: Google PhD Fellowship Program
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The 2026 cycle ran 5 March to 30 April 2026 and is closed. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: Region-dependent: US/Canada up to ~$85K/year (2 yrs); India up to $50K (4 yrs); Europe yearly bursary; SE Asia $10K/year (3 yrs); Africa/LatAm ~$15K/year (2-3 yrs)
grants.description: University-nominated PhD fellowship for outstanding graduate students in CS and related fields, including machine learning, systems, HCI, quantum, health research, and algorithms. Includes Google research mentor.

grants.name: Microsoft Research Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: The last call opened 4 November 2025 and closed 16 December 2025. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.region: Global (Africa, Asia, Australia/NZ, Canada, Europe, Latin America, US)
grants.amount: $17,000-$47,000 (region-dependent), unrestricted gift
grants.description: Funded collaboration with Microsoft Research on open research challenges for PhD students, postdocs, and faculty. Replaces the earlier MSR PhD Fellowship and Research Fellows India programs as a unified global program.

grants.name: Amazon Research Awards (ARA)
grants.deadlineNote: Fall 2026 call closes 23:59 Pacific Time on 4 November 2026. One proposal per PI per call period. PI must be full-time faculty at an accredited institution or a permanent researcher at a legally recognised non-profit/NGO.
grants.amount: Unrestricted institutional gift (cash plus AWS promotional credits); funding and credits vary by research area, see the call page for per-topic ceilings
grants.description: Funds academic and non-profit researchers across nine areas including agentic AI, information security, automated reasoning, cryptography, multilingual AI evaluation, multimodal perception, and AWS Trainium. Awardees receive an Amazon research contact and training resources.

grants.name: AWS Cloud Credit for Research
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling submissions; reviews on 90-120 day cycles
grants.amount: Up to $5,000 students; uncapped for faculty/staff
grants.description: AWS promotional credits for finite research projects to build cloud-hosted services, develop repeatable solutions, or migrate research processes/open data to the cloud.

grants.name: Meta Research PhD Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: Meta's page says it is not accepting new applications. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: $42,000/year stipend + full tuition and fees
grants.description: Supports PhD students across AR/VR, AI, HCI, privacy, networking, programming languages, statistics, and related areas aligned with Meta's research. Includes travel funding for a research summit.

grants.name: NVIDIA Graduate Fellowship Program
grants.deadlineNote: The 2027-28 call is open; applications and recommendation letters are due 30 October 2026.
grants.amount: Up to $60,000 per student
grants.description: Fellowship for PhD students who have completed at least their first year, focused on GPU computing, AI/ML, graphics, robotics, autonomous vehicles, HPC, and related areas. Requires a mandatory in-person NVIDIA Research internship.

grants.name: NVIDIA Academic Grant Program (Hardware/Compute)
grants.deadlineNote: Program currently not accepting new applications as of 2026; check page for future submission windows.
grants.amount: Up to 30,000 H100 80GB GPU-hours, RTX PRO 6000 GPUs, or DGX Spark systems
grants.description: Cloud GPU hours, hardware donations, and software for university faculty researching scientific simulation, quantum computing, physics-informed ML, AI training, and AI inference/agents. Proposals must incorporate NVIDIA models or software.

grants.name: Adobe Research Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: Applications are closed and the 2026 fellows have been announced. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: INR 12,00,000 stipend (India AI Research Fellowship)
grants.description: Recognizes outstanding graduate students conducting research in AI/ML, computer vision, NLP, HCI, graphics, audio, and document intelligence. Includes salaried Adobe Research internship and an Adobe mentor.

grants.name: IBM PhD Fellowship Awards
grants.deadlineNote: IBM has paused the 2026-2027 PhD Fellowship Program and will make no new awards this cycle. IBM plans to announce a new program in the first quarter of 2027.
grants.amount: US universities: $40,000; other countries: $6,000-$25,000 (varies by country)
grants.duration: Fall/Spring academic year (renewable in some cases)

grants.deadlineNote: Proposals are invited through universities that hold an MoU with RGSTC, each with its own call dates. RGSTC also runs the CPIITA scheme for institution-industry projects.
grants.description: State S&T grants for innovative applications of science and technology aimed at socio-economic development of Maharashtra. Open to R&D institutions, universities, and colleges in the state. CPIITA scheme supports academia-industry collaborative technology development/adoption.

grants.name: Bharat Life Sciences Awards 2026
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026 application window closed 10 August 2026. Check the funder's site for a 2027 edition.
grants.amount: INR 7 crore total grant pool across six categories
grants.description: Awards recognising excellence in healthcare and life sciences across two streams: Samman (Grants) - Ramanujan Arogya Udaan (Young Scientist), Charaka (Innovation for Unmet Patient Needs), Sushruta (Translational and Clinical Advancement), Nalanda (Institute of Scientific Excellence); and Gaurav (Recognition) - Jivaka (Healthcare/Life Sciences Startup Innovator) and Sarabhai (Promoting Scientific Ecosystem in India). Open to researchers, scientists, public research institutions, universities, and private-sector innovators.

grants.name: Tinker Research and Teaching Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling; applications assessed within a week. Teaching Grants provide $250 in Tinker credits per student for academic classes.
grants.amount: Research Grants from USD 5,000 in Tinker credits/funding; Teaching Grants USD 250/student
grants.description: Grants for researchers, students, and instructors whose work involves training or teaching with open-weight LLMs via Tinker. Recent recipients include fine-tuning small-molecule chemistry models (Grant Rotskoff, Stanford) and CMU Deep RL coursework (Aviral Kumar, Katerina Fragkiadaki).

grants.name: Interactivity Research Grants
grants.deadlineNote: 2026 cycle closed 19 June 2026. Next call TBD.
grants.amount: USD 100,000 + USD 25,000 in Tinker credits per award
grants.description: Multi-award RFP on human-AI interactivity. Four focus areas: real-time multimodal interaction evaluations, safety for multimodal systems, generative UI for explaining complex information, and human steering of agents during extended tasks. Also accepts proposals on any topic advancing interactivity in AI.

grants.name: Emergent Ventures
grants.funder: Mercatus Center at George Mason University
grants.deadlineNote: No deadlines listed. Besides the general program there are tranches for Africa and the Caribbean, archaeology, India, career travel, U.K. dynamism, Ukraine, and U.S. science policy. Ages 13+.
grants.region: Global (with India, Africa/Caribbean, Ukraine, AI verticals)
grants.amount: Flexible; from modest sums to substantial awards
grants.description: Low-overhead fellowship and grant program for entrepreneurs and researchers pursuing highly scalable 'zero to one' ideas including scientific research, deep tech, AI, biotech, and metascience. No application fee; no strings attached.

grants.name: ACX Grants
grants.funder: Astral Codex Ten (Scott Alexander) via Manifund
grants.deadlineNote: The 2025 round closed 15 August 2025. The organiser hopes to run further rounds; no 2026 round has been announced.
grants.amount: Typically USD 5,000-50,000; rare grants up to USD 100,000; ~USD 1 million total per round
grants.description: Microgrants for charitable or scientific projects surfaced through the Astral Codex Ten community. Prior rounds funded biomedical research, AI safety, biosecurity, forecasting, and metascience. Administered by Manifund.

grants.name: gradCapital Atomic Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: Apply through the form on the funder's page; no deadline is stated.
grants.amount: USD 1,000-5,000 no-strings grant; USD 60,000 (alongside classes) or USD 300,000 (full-time) project funding
grants.description: Micro-grant for students pursuing independent science and engineering projects outside traditional academic constraints. Engineering-heavy ideas with real-world potential are prioritised.

grants.name: Bambu Lab Let's Make It Fund
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling; two to five projects selected per quarter. Age 18+ (or age of majority in home jurisdiction). No requirement to own a Bambu Lab printer.
grants.amount: From a few thousand USD up to USD 300,000
grants.description: Grants for ambitious maker projects across hardware, engineering, education, and open manufacturing. Evaluated on originality, positive impact, and feasibility. Includes financial support plus technical guidance and promotion.

grants.name: 1517 Medici Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling; apply via a five-minute Loom video. No-strings-attached (no IP/equity claims). Currently North America only.
grants.amount: Minimum USD 1,000 stipend
grants.description: Microgrants for high school students, college students, dropouts, and 'renegade' deep-tech scientists pursuing science, engineering, mathematics, or heretical technical passion projects outside academic credit.

grants.name: O'Shaughnessy Fellowships & Grants
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026 cycle closed on 30 April 2026. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: USD 100,000 (Fellowship, 10 per year) or USD 10,000+ (Grant, 20+ per year)
grants.description: Equity-free, IP-free, one-year fellowship for researchers, builders, and creatives across science, engineering, and adjacent fields. Requires 40-60 hours/week commitment. No education/nationality requirements.

grants.name: Alive Prize
grants.funder: Alive Prize (partners include Solcoa Industries, Shinkei Systems, Splunk founders)
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling deadline; the application takes under 10 minutes and decisions come within two weeks.
grants.amount: USD 100,000 (uncapped)
grants.description: Grant for young people (high school through PhD, including dropouts) building projects that push humanity forward. Past recipients have worked on human brain organoids for Alzheimer's research, extreme-heat resilience, and stable antibody design.

grants.name: Thiel Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling annual applications; two-year program. Age 22 or younger; must drop out or defer college to accept.
grants.amount: USD 250,000 over two years (raised from USD 100,000 for the 2026 class)
grants.description: Two-year fellowship for young founders building deep tech, science, AI, biotech, and hardware companies instead of continuing formal education. Alumni include founders of Anthropic, Figma, and Ethereum.

grants.name: 776 Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: The 2025 round closed in April 2025. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: Up to USD 100,000 over two years
grants.description: Fellowship for young people building solutions to climate change and environmental issues - clean tech, adaptation, resilience, and sustainability. Includes access to the 776 network of entrepreneurs and investors.

grants.name: Global Health and Wellbeing in an Era of Transformative AI (RFP)
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling review ran through 21 August 2026. Check the funder's site for current status.
grants.amount: USD 10M-30M program pool; per-grant USD <100K to USD 10M
grants.description: Funds research, policy, implementation, field-building, institutions, and infrastructure to help ensure transformative AI improves human health and wellbeing, with particular attention to risks for and benefits to the global poor. Distinct from 'AI for good' projects that just apply AI as a tool - this RFP targets the larger implications of AI transforming the world.

grants.name: Cohere Labs Scholars Program
grants.deadlineNote: Applications are closed. The funder says it is revising the programme and that applications are expected to open in Fall 2026; no deadline is posted.
grants.description: Paid research residency for emerging researchers in NLP and machine learning. Targets candidates with strong engineering skills and creative thinking but limited or no prior publication experience. No previous research experience required.

grants.name: Cohere Labs Catalyst Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling. Grants provide API access to Cohere models rather than cash.
grants.amount: API credits to Cohere models
grants.description: API-access grants for academic partners, civic organisations, and public-impact groups. Focus areas: language model safety, prosocial LM applications (education, climate science, content moderation, healthcare, law, history, social science), and language model capabilities.

grants.name: Turing AI Global Fellowships
grants.funder: The Alan Turing Institute / UKRI EPSRC
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026 round opened 18 November 2025 and closed 12 March 2026; fellowships must start by 1 February 2027. UKRI has not announced another round.
grants.amount: Up to GBP 4.5 million per award + up to 1,000,000 GPU hours per fellow via UK AI Research Resource (AIRR)
grants.description: Fellowship for exceptional, world-class AI experts based outside the UK - either established international leaders or those with outstanding potential - to relocate to a UK host institution. Part of the GBP 46 million Turing AI Fellowships programme.

grants.name: Vector Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellows
grants.deadlineNote: Two intakes a year: spring cohort applications are due 28 February and autumn cohort applications 31 August, at 23:59 EST.
grants.description: Postdoctoral fellowship at Vector Institute for fundamental machine-learning and deep-learning research (theory and applications). Fellows propose independent research and collaborate with 1-2 of Vector's 45+ ML/DL faculty; can engage in teaching, mentoring, and entrepreneurial activities.

grants.name: Hugging Face Community GPU Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling. Apply from the hardware section of a Space's Settings page.
grants.amount: GPU compute allocations on Hugging Face Spaces
grants.description: Free GPU compute (A10G, T4, or larger) for academic and open-source projects hosted as Hugging Face Spaces. Supports research demos, model releases, and community tools. ZeroGPU is available for free within quota; PRO and Team/Enterprise members get 8x the standard quota.

grants.name: Templeton Diverse Intelligences Initiative
grants.funder: Templeton World Charity Foundation and John Templeton Foundation
grants.deadlineNote: TWCF's Diverse Intelligences page lists no open call. Related small grants and workshops are run through the TWCF-funded Global Research Centre for Diverse Intelligences at St Andrews. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: Varies (initiative pool: USD 60M+ over 3 years across all Templeton intelligence grants)
grants.description: Cross-disciplinary programme to study intelligence in animal, human, and machine systems. Themes: diversity of intelligence (biological systems), plurality of intelligence (collective and distributed), and future of intelligence (machine and AI trajectory and ethics). Open to philosophers, ethicists, biologists, neuroscientists, physicists, computer scientists.

grants.name: Mila Postdoctoral Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling; opportunities arise year-round depending on lab needs. Applicants must be invited by a Mila faculty member. Within 5 years of PhD.
grants.description: Postdoctoral positions in the lab of a Mila professor covering deep learning, reinforcement learning, NLP, computer vision, ML theory, and AI safety/policy. Also runs the separate Mila AI Policy Fellowship (French-language cohort starting September 2026).

grants.name: National Quantum Mission (NQM) Calls for Proposals
grants.funder: Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: The startup call has been rolling since 15 July 2025, with applications made through the relevant Thematic Hub. The 2025 quantum algorithms and undergraduate teaching lab calls were time-bound; check DST for new NQM calls.
grants.description: National mission to make India a leader in quantum technologies. Funds research and startups across quantum computing, communication, sensing/metrology, and materials/devices. Watch DST call-for-proposals portal and individual T-Hub websites.

grants.name: NM-ICPS Technology Innovation Hubs (TIHs)
grants.funder: Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: 25 Technology Innovation Hubs (TIHs) hosted at IITs, IISc, IIITs, and NITs each run their own calls for research grants, fellowships (Chanakya UG/PG/PDF), startup grants (TIDE, TIH-SEED, PRISM), and hackathons. Watch individual TIH portals.
grants.amount: Rs 3,660 crore total mission outlay; per-award varies by TIH
grants.description: National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems umbrella. 25 TIHs cover AI, machine learning, robotics, cybersecurity, data science, quantum technologies, IoT, autonomous systems, and CPS. Over 6,400 fellowships awarded to date.

grants.name: NBHM Postdoctoral Fellowship (Mathematics)
grants.funder: National Board for Higher Mathematics (NBHM), Department of Atomic Energy
grants.deadlineNote: Two cycles per year: Autumn (30 June deadline) and Spring (31 December deadline). Applicants must be under 35.
grants.description: Postdoctoral fellowship for young mathematicians (below 35) with PhD in mathematics (or thesis submitted). Tenable at Indian universities and research institutions.

grants.name: Dr. D.S. Kothari Postdoctoral Fellowship in Sciences
grants.funder: University Grants Commission (UGC), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling; selection within ~6 weeks. Age limit typically 35 (with relaxations). Tenable only at UGC-supported science departments of Indian universities and UGC-funded inter-university centres (IUCAA, IUAC, UGC-DAE-CSR, etc.).
grants.amount: INR 67,000/month + INR 1,00,000/year contingency (revised 1 January 2024)
grants.description: Postdoctoral fellowship for PhD holders in the sciences, established in 2007 in honour of Dr. Daulat Singh Kothari, UGC's first Chairman.

grants.name: Atal Incubation Centres (AIC)
grants.deadlineNote: AIM states the AIC application portal is not currently open. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: Grant-in-aid up to INR 10 crore per AIC
grants.description: Establishes greenfield incubation centres to nurture innovative startups. Covers capital and operational expenditure, sectoral mentoring, seed capital access, industry partnerships, and training.

grants.name: CSIR Research Associateship (RA)
grants.deadlineNote: Applications invited annually through all-India press advertisement. Upper age 35 (5-year relaxation for SC/ST/PWD/women; 3-year for OBC non-creamy layer). Requires at least one publication in a refereed journal listed in Journal Citation Reports.
grants.amount: INR 58,000 / 61,000 / 67,000 per month (three tiers; selection committee may place awardees in higher tier with justification)
grants.description: Postdoctoral research associateship for young researchers (PhD in science/engineering, MD/MS/MDS, or ME/MTech/MPharm/MVSc with 3 years R&D experience) working on specific projects at CSIR labs and other research institutions.

grants.name: CSIR-Nehru Science Postdoctoral Research Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call via CSIR-HRDG; watch csirhrdg.res.in for announcements.
grants.description: Postdoctoral fellowship named for Jawaharlal Nehru, supporting outstanding early-career researchers to work in CSIR labs across chemistry, biology, physics, engineering, and applied sciences.

grants.name: SPARC - Scheme for Promotion of Academic and Research Collaboration
grants.funder: Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: Proposal submission is currently closed; the SPARC portal says it is likely to open soon. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: Up to INR 1 crore per project
grants.description: Joint research projects between top Indian HEIs and globally ranked foreign institutions, with mobility of faculty and students. High-impact themes include AI, quantum, MedTech, climate, semiconductors, and smart cities.

grants.name: DRDO Extramural Research and Intellectual Property Rights (ER&IPR)
grants.funder: Directorate of Extramural Research and Intellectual Property Rights, DRDO
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling. Proposals submitted online via the Electronic Project Proposal Management System (EPPMS) and reviewed by DRDO lab experts and academic reviewers.
grants.amount: Project-based
grants.description: Extramural grants to Indian universities, colleges, research institutions, and industry R&D groups for basic and applied research in defence-relevant sciences and engineering. Also supports Centres of Excellence, infrastructure, and workshops/symposia.

grants.name: DBT Research Associateship (DBT-RA)
grants.funder: Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call through the Common Fellowship Portal; the 2025-26 call closed in May 2026. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.duration: 2 years (extendable up to 4 based on progress)
grants.description: Postdoctoral training for young researchers in biotechnology and life sciences at premier Indian research institutions, universities, and non-profit R&D bodies. Open to PhD holders in science or engineering, or MD/MS in medicine, with research interests in biotech/life sciences.

grants.name: BIRAC SITARE-GYTI Award Grant
grants.deadlineNote: Annual cycle; the GYTI-2025 call closed in January 2026. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: Up to INR 15 lakh per project (15 projects funded per cycle)
grants.description: Student Innovations for Translation & Advancement of Research Explorations (SITARE) award for Indian PhD/Masters students working on translational innovations across healthcare, life sciences, diagnostics, medical devices, drugs, vaccines, industrial biotech, bioinformatics, agriculture, waste management, sanitation, clean energy, and AI/IoT applications in these areas.

grants.name: AICTE Research Promotion Scheme (RPS) - Lab to Market
grants.funder: All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE)
grants.deadlineNote: The scheme now runs as RPS Lab to Market; the 2025 round closed in July 2025. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: Up to INR 25 lakh per project
grants.description: Extramural research grants in engineering sciences and emerging technologies. Restructured as 'RPS: Lab to Market' with focus on AI, machine learning, quantum computing and communication, and big data. Supports both research and Master's/PhD student generation to augment faculty quality.

grants.name: IndoML Datathon 2026 - Indic Speech Noise Detection & Removal
grants.funder: IndoML (Heritage Institute of Technology, IIT Kharagpur, IISc Bangalore, Inception - G42)
grants.deadlineNote: Registration closed 9 September 2026 and final submissions closed 17 October 2026. Top teams present at IndoML 2026 at IIT Kharagpur in December 2026.
grants.amount: INR 2,00,000 total prize pool
grants.description: Research-oriented data-science competition on noise event detection and removal in real-world Indic speech. Two tracks: (1) identify noise events with precise timestamps, (2) suppress detected noise while preserving speech intelligibility. Uses ~150 hours of real-world Indic audio from the Vaani corpus. At least one team member must be affiliated with an Indian university or research institution.

grants.name: Flipkart GRiD
grants.deadlineNote: Annual competition; GRiD 8.0 (2026) registration closed 7 July 2026. Check the funder's site for the next season.
grants.amount: Cash prizes + SDE interview / offer pathways; top offers up to INR 32.67 LPA
grants.description: India-wide engineering and SDE challenge across Software Development, AI Engineering, and Data Science tracks solving real-world e-commerce problems. Open to B.Tech/B.E./M.Tech/M.E./M.S./PhD/Dual/Integrated Degree students at recognised Indian institutions. Online rounds + National Finals at Flipkart Bengaluru HQ.

grants.name: HackOn With Amazon
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. Season 6 registrations closed 28 May 2026. Check the funder's site for the next season.
grants.amount: INR 2.25 lakh prize pool + Pre-Placement Interview (PPI) opportunities
grants.description: Amazon India's flagship engineering hackathon. Multi-round format (coding challenge, 48-hour hackathon, mentorship, grand finale). Eligibility for Season 6: B.Tech/M.Tech/MCA graduates of 2026/2027 with CGPA >=6.5.

grants.name: HackWithInfy
grants.deadlineNote: Annual; 2026 registrations opened 6 February 2026. Check the funder's site for the next cycle.
grants.amount: Cash prizes + Pre-Placement Interviews and internship opportunities
grants.description: Infosys' flagship pan-India hackathon for engineering students. Designed to identify and nurture strong programming talent and route participants to Infosys PPIs and internships.

grants.name: TCS CodeVita
grants.deadlineNote: Season 14 registration is open. The official site does not list the registration deadline or round dates; check codevita.tcsapps.com.
grants.amount: USD 20,000 shared by the top 3 coders; finalists may travel to India for the Grand Finale
grants.description: Open-book, six-hour coding competition open to undergraduate students worldwide. Teams of 1-3 solve problems of varying complexity across multiple online rounds culminating in a global finale.

grants.name: ChatGPT for Academic Researchers
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling. Rolling out to 10,000 researchers first, expanding to 100,000 through 2027. Apply via form on OpenAI's site with institutional affiliation and research use case.
grants.region: Global (recognised degree-granting institutions with high research activity)
grants.amount: Free access to frontier models across ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex (including GPT-5.6 at launch); business-grade privacy; data not used for training by default; invite up to 4 institutional collaborators
grants.description: Part of OpenAI's USD 250M+ commitment through 2027 to support external scientific research. Free frontier-model access for researchers at recognised colleges and universities, aimed at accelerating scientific discovery.

grants.name: ANRF PAIR - Partnerships for Accelerated Innovation and Research
grants.deadlineNote: Calls are announced on the ANRF portal. The hub submits on behalf of a network of 3 to 7 spokes. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: Up to INR 100 crore over five years per hub-and-spoke network
grants.description: Mentorship-driven hub-and-spoke programme to grow research capacity across Indian universities. Hub: top-25 NIRF overall or top 26-50 INIs. Spokes: central/state public universities (top 200 NIRF), NITs/IIITs, or other central/state public universities. At least two state public universities per network mandatory; at least one spoke outside the hub's state.

grants.name: ANRF Inclusivity Research Grant (IRG)
grants.deadlineNote: 2026 window closes 3 November 2026. Subsumes the earlier EMEQ scheme. For Indian nationals in SC/ST categories in regular academic or lab positions. Applicants must have at least four years of service remaining, no ongoing IRG or EMEQ project, and apply without a co-investigator.
grants.amount: Up to INR 60 lakh excluding institutional overheads
grants.description: Research grant for SC/ST scientists to conduct frontier research in science and engineering at Indian academic institutions, national labs, and recognised R&D organisations. Includes flexible recurring support plus international travel and publication or patent costs. Open to PhD-holders in Science or Engineering and MD/MS/MDS.

grants.name: COLD Winter School 2026 - Complexity, Optimisation, Learning, Dynamics
grants.funder: Centre for Complex Systems and Dynamics, IIT Madras (with Office of Global Engagement)
grants.deadlineNote: Applications closed 31 August 2026 and the school is full. It runs 10-15 December 2026 at IIT Madras.
grants.amount: Fully funded (registration INR 1,000+GST; up to 3-tier AC train fare reimbursed; on-campus accommodation and meals provided)
grants.description: Six-day intensive winter school for late-UG and Master's students in engineering, mathematics, physics, or CS. Fifteen lectures across four interconnected themes: Complexity (computational tractability), Optimisation (convex analysis, gradient methods), Learning (statistical learning theory, neural networks), and Dynamics (nonlinear systems, chaos). Plus research projects and lab visits. Prerequisites: linear algebra, multivariable calculus, basic probability, Python.

grants.name: Sony Research Award Program 2026
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call; the 2026 round ran from 15 July to 15 September 2026 and is closed. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: Up to USD 100,000 (Faculty Innovation) or USD 150,000 (Focused Research)
grants.description: Academia-industry collaboration awards for cutting-edge research in AI, robotics, sensing, imaging, sustainability, and entertainment technologies. 2026 focus areas include mechanistic interpretability of LLMs/MLLMs, speech/audio models, music models, and video generation for multimodal content.

grants.name: Anthropic Claude Science Grants
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026 round closed 15 July 2026; projects run 1 September to 1 December 2026. No further round has been announced.
grants.amount: Up to USD 30,000 in Claude API credits + up to USD 2,000 Modal compute (select recipients)
grants.description: Grants supporting scientific research that uses Claude, with emphasis on biology and biomedical research but open to all scientific domains. Eligible: academic researchers, independent scientists, biotech startups.

grants.name: Anthropic AI for Science - Rare Disease Research Track
grants.deadlineNote: The rare disease call closed 2 August 2026. Anthropic plans further thematic calls within the AI for Science program; check the funder's site.
grants.amount: Up to USD 50,000 in Claude API credits
grants.description: Themed sub-grant within Anthropic's AI for Science program for researchers and early-stage biotechs working on rare genetic diseases. Uses Claude for scientific discovery, hypothesis generation, and data analysis in a domain with under-served patient populations.

grants.name: Amgen Scholars Program
grants.deadlineNote: Summer 2027 applications open 1 November 2026 for Europe, the United States, Asia, and Canada; the Australia round has closed. Deadlines are set by each regional programme.
grants.region: USA, EU, Australia, Japan, Singapore (host institutions)
grants.amount: Housing + stipend + travel to annual Amgen Scholars Symposium
grants.description: Undergraduate summer research programme in science and biotechnology hosted at leading universities globally (Harvard, MIT, Columbia, Berkeley, Stanford, Cambridge, Karolinska, Tokyo, Kyoto, LMU Munich, NUS, and others). Each host runs its own selection process.

grants.name: DBT-BUILDER - Boost to University Interdisciplinary Life Science Departments for Education and Research
grants.funder: Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: No call is open on DBT's call-for-proposals page. Check that page for the next round.
grants.amount: Multi-crore institutional support (infrastructure + operational)
grants.description: Flagship DBT programme to establish interdisciplinary Schools of Life Sciences at Indian universities. Funds infrastructure, equipment, and human-resource development to strengthen postgraduate-level education and research in life sciences at central/state universities.

grants.name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS)
grants.funder: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling applications through DPIIT-recognised incubators; 2026 startup-application window closed 31 May 2026. Priority sectors: agriculture, biotech, energy, education, health, water, and other innovation-heavy domains. Startup must be DPIIT-recognised, <=2 years old, with >=51% Indian shareholding.
grants.amount: Up to INR 20 lakh (proof-of-concept / prototype / product trials) or up to INR 50 lakh (commercialisation)
grants.description: Seed funding for early-stage startups routed through approved incubators (not directly to applicants). Incubators must be operational for 2+ years with facilities for 25+ seats and 5+ incubatees at time of application.

grants.name: HFSP Research Grants (Program & Early Career)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call. The current round's LOI closed 26 March 2026 and invited full proposals were due in mid-September 2026. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: USD 300K/year (2-member), 400K/year (3-member), or 500K/year (4-member team)
grants.description: Frontier research grants for interdisciplinary multinational teams tackling fundamental biological problems. Two tracks: Program Grants (any career stage) and Early Career Research Grants (all team members within 5 years of first independent position). No preliminary data required at LOI stage.

grants.name: WCS Research Fellowship Program
grants.deadlineNote: WCS states the programme is not currently accepting applications. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.region: Global South (with Native American / First Nations exception)
grants.amount: Up to USD 15,000
grants.description: Small grants for individual field research projects with clear application to conservation of threatened wildlife and wild places. Priority themes include business and conservation, climate change, ecosystem services, human wellbeing, and wildlife health.

grants.name: BSF Research Grants (US-Israel)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual mid-November deadline; each scientific discipline is eligible only every other year. 2026 (even year) supports chemistry, computer sciences, earth/ocean/atmospheric sciences, economics, energy, environmental, materials, mathematical sciences, physics, sociology/anthropology, and psychology (excluding psychobiology).
grants.amount: Typical annual awards USD 25-55K per side (up to USD 300,000 total over 4 years, experimental)
grants.description: Grants for joint research by U.S. and Israeli PIs; no prior collaboration required but scientific synergy must be evident. Companion NSF-BSF track lets US applicants apply through NSF programs with a joint BSF-funded Israeli partner.

grants.name: Wallenberg Scholars
grants.deadlineNote: By university nomination only; there is no open call for individuals. Check the funder's site for the next round.
grants.amount: SEK 18 million (theoretical) or SEK 20 million (experimental)
grants.description: Long-term free-use funding for Sweden's leading senior researchers in medicine, technology, and natural sciences. Broader Foundation portfolio also includes Wallenberg Academy Fellows (early-career) and project grants; the Foundation disburses ~SEK 2+ billion per year across programmes.

grants.name: NIDHI PRAYAS 2.0
grants.funder: Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: Students and innovators apply through NIDHI-PRAYAS Centres (at selected Technology Business Incubators). 2026 centre-selection window closed 30 June 2026; ongoing intake at operational PRAYAS Centres.
grants.amount: Up to INR 20 lakh per innovator/startup for prototyping (Level 1 Centre)
grants.description: DST flagship for young innovators and early-stage startups to convert science and technology ideas into working physical prototypes. Sector-agnostic; PRAYAS 2.0 adds enhanced support for deep-tech innovations.

grants.name: Rolex Awards for Enterprise
grants.deadlineNote: The 2027 application cycle closed on 17 October 2026. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: CHF 200,000 for laureates + associate awards
grants.description: Awards for individuals with innovative, ongoing projects in science and health, the environment, applied technology, exploration, or cultural heritage. Part of Rolex's Perpetual Planet Initiative.

grants.name: Google Center for Climate Tech Call for Proposals 2026
grants.funder: Google and the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India (Manthan-Utthan)
grants.deadlineNote: Listed on the Manthan-Utthan platform (sign-in required to view) with a cut-off of 27 November 2026.
grants.amount: Up to INR 4.72 crore
grants.description: Technology-driven proposals for a national climate-technology hub focused on water optimisation and advanced waste management. Priority areas: wastewater treatment, water harvesting, natural-source mapping, industrial cooling efficiency, e-waste systems, high-efficiency recycling, intelligent waste platforms, and circular-resource management. Aims to accelerate deployable solutions and strengthen government-industry-research collaboration.

grants.name: Tiny Blue Dot Foundation - Perception Box Research (Round 5)
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026 RFP is closed; letters of intent were due 5 October 2026. Invited applicants submit full proposals by 25 February 2027.
grants.region: Global (recognised universities and non-profit research institutions)
grants.amount: Up to USD 900,000 total including up to 15% overhead
grants.description: Rigorous, empirical research on the Perception Box: how expectations, beliefs, bodily signals, and social experience shape perceived reality, behaviour, and mental wellbeing. 2026 focus areas: agency and independence, interoception and emotional regulation, identity and self-narrative, and values, meaning, and belonging. Neural, psychological, somatic, or technology-enabled interventions welcomed.

grants.name: India AMR Co-Development Programme (I-AMR-CDP)
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling review of non-confidential expressions of interest through 31 October 2026. Selected innovators enter a co-development agreement with Venus Remedies via a mutually agreed value-sharing model.
grants.amount: INR 10 lakh upfront award on entering a co-development agreement, plus Venus-led development investment
grants.description: Co-development call for promising Indian anti-infective innovations at proof-of-concept or preclinical stage: novel antibiotics, beta-lactamase inhibitors, or adjunctive/potentiator therapies. Selected teams receive end-to-end development, R&D infrastructure, manufacturing, commercialisation, IP, and publication support. Open to academic institutions, industry researchers, startups or spin-outs, and independent investigators in India.

grants.name: Shwas Kavach: AI-Enabled Decentralised National Medical Oxygen Grid
grants.funder: Newttorr Pumps and Systems Private Limited (via Manthan-Utthan, PSA India)
grants.deadlineNote: Launched 23 April 2026; applications close 22 December 2026 via the Manthan-Utthan platform.
grants.description: R&D innovations call under the National Medical Oxygen Grid roadmap. Areas include AI-driven demand forecasting, IoT-enabled real-time monitoring, district-level containerised oxygen generation units, geospatial mapping for supply chains, oxygen cylinder banks for last-mile delivery, and a digital twin for simulation and emergency preparedness. 18-month roadmap from pilot to national scale.

grants.name: CHT Expression of Interest: Mission-Oriented Technology Development
grants.funder: Centre for High Technology (CHT), Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: Launched 29 June 2026 via Manthan-Utthan; applications close 31 December 2026. Industry market-ready innovation track.
grants.description: EOI for mission-oriented technology development in the hydrocarbon sector: refinery processes, petroleum products, catalysts, and technology modernisation. CHT is the technology cell of the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, chartered to build indigenous capability and self-reliance.

grants.name: HHMI Hanna H. Gray Fellows Program
grants.deadlineNote: The 2028 competition, combined with the Freeman Hrabowski Scholars, opens 3 November 2026 and closes 15 December 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. The competition runs every other year.
grants.amount: USD 80,000 salary + USD 20,000 expense allowance per year
grants.description: Postdoc-to-faculty transition programme for early-career scientists from historically excluded backgrounds pursuing careers in the biomedical and life sciences. Multi-phase support carries fellows from postdoc through faculty appointment.

grants.name: NIH Pathway to Independence Award (K99/R00)
grants.deadlineNote: Standard due dates: 12 February, 12 June, 12 October for new applications; 12 March, 12 July, 12 November for resubmissions. NCI no longer participates in this announcement and uses its own K99/R00 NOFOs.
grants.region: United States (with international postdoc eligibility for some institutes)
grants.amount: K99 phase up to USD 90K/yr salary + research costs; R00 phase up to USD 249K/yr direct costs
grants.duration: K99: up to 2 years (mentored); R00: up to 3 years (independent)
grants.description: Two-phase award to accelerate promising postdocs to tenure-track independent research positions. Mentored K99 phase followed by independent R00 phase activated upon a faculty appointment. Companion Independent Clinical Trial Allowed track (PA-24-193) available.

grants.name: UGC Faculty Recharge Programme (UGC-FRP)
grants.funder: University Grants Commission (UGC), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling / periodic calls. Positions at Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, and Professor levels. Compensation at par with Central University appointees. NET/PhD required.
grants.description: Inducts outstanding candidates into Indian universities in basic sciences (Physics, Mathematics, Chemistry, Biology) and Engineering and Earth Sciences, at faculty levels, to strengthen research and teaching in interdisciplinary and frontier areas.

grants.name: Klingenstein Fellowship Awards in Neuroscience
grants.deadlineNote: Annual cycle; deadline 1 February. Previously the Klingenstein-Simons partnership (2013-2024); now run solely by the Klingenstein Fund. For early-career tenure-track investigators in basic or clinical neuroscience.
grants.amount: USD 150,000 per year (USD 450,000 total)
grants.description: Supports high-risk, high-reward projects by early-career investigators in cellular and molecular neuroscience, neural systems, and translational research on neurological and psychiatric disorders. Funds may be used for salary, research assistants, equipment, or any research-related purpose.

grants.name: AASM Foundation Strategic Research Grant
grants.funder: American Academy of Sleep Medicine Foundation
grants.deadlineNote: The letter of intent deadline was 19 October 2026; invited full applications are due 8 March 2027. Three categories: I (up to USD 250K), II (up to USD 100K), III (up to USD 50K).
grants.amount: Cat-I up to USD 250,000; Cat-II up to USD 100,000; Cat-III up to USD 50,000
grants.description: Investigator-initiated research addressing gaps in patient-centred diagnosis and care for sleep disorders. Recent cycles have prioritised obstructive sleep apnea research gaps, AASM strategic-plan goals, dissemination and implementation research, and sleep health disparities.

grants.name: Clean Air Fund - Black Carbon Reduction in Cold-Climate LMICs
grants.deadlineNote: Expressions of interest closed 23 October 2026. Check the funder's site for future calls.
grants.description: Field studies measuring real-world black-carbon reductions and associated health and climate benefits from cleaner space-heating or industrial interventions in inhabited cold-climate regions of low- and middle-income countries. Projects should assess emissions under actual use, health and climate outcomes, and, where possible, community acceptance.

grants.name: Conservation, Food & Health Foundation Grants Program
grants.deadlineNote: Two concept-application windows each year: 15 October to 22 December and 1 May to 15 June. Invited applicants then submit full proposals.
grants.amount: No formal min/max; most grants USD 25,000-50,000 per year
grants.description: Applied research, pilot projects, training, and technical assistance in developing regions across three priorities: biodiversity and climate resilience, sustainable agriculture and food systems, and community-level public health. Open to universities, non-profits, NGOs, and civil-society and community-based organisations.

grants.name: Program for the Archiving of Science and Technology (PAST) - Cohort 2
grants.funder: Archives at NCBS, National Centre for Biological Sciences
grants.deadlineNote: Cohort 2 applications closed 23 October 2026. Final projects are announced 15 January 2027 and run 1 February 2027 to 31 January 2028.
grants.amount: Up to INR 12,00,000 (inclusive of all taxes)
grants.description: Twelve-month projects to identify, appraise, describe, digitise, and preserve at-risk archival material relating to the history of science and technology in India from roughly 1850 to 2000. Priority for rare, endangered, underrepresented, or marginalised STEM histories. Includes structured archival training and expert guidance.

grants.name: UGC-DAE CSR Collaborative Research Scheme 2026
grants.deadlineNote: The CRS 2026 call closed 22 October 2026 (extended from 15 October). Check the CSR user portal for the next call.
grants.amount: In-kind facility access plus travel and local support
grants.description: Three-year collaborative research using UGC-DAE CSR in-house instruments or major DAE facilities, including synchrotrons at RRCAT, the Dhruva reactor at BARC, the cyclotron at VECC, IGCAR facilities, and centre-specific advanced instruments. Open to permanent faculty at UGC-approved or NAAC-accredited institutions and scientists at Government of India-recognised research bodies.

grants.name: Global Brain Care Scholars Program
grants.funder: Ban Ki-moon Foundation, Paris Brain Institute, and Vascular Brain Health Institute
grants.deadlineNote: Applications opened in September 2026; the winter school in Paris is in January 2027 and the local project runs February to June 2027. Check the funder's site for the application status.
grants.amount: Full cost coverage for the Paris winter school; EUR 800 seed grant on project approval; additional conference support for top three scholars
grants.description: Twelve-month hybrid scholarship for ten young professionals working on prevention of stroke, dementia, and depression in underserved communities. Includes a fully funded Paris winter school, virtual workshops, mentoring, and a seed grant for a localised Changemaker Project. Applicants aged 20-35 with a master's degree, B2 English, and relevant experience in brain-health research, care, advocacy, policy, or digital innovation.

grants.name: Company of Biologists Travelling Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: Four rounds a year; upcoming deadlines are 5 February, 7 May, 6 August and 5 November 2027. Visits must occur within six months of the funding decision and cannot have started before it.
grants.amount: Up to GBP 3,000
grants.duration: Single collaborative visit within 6 months of decision
grants.description: Travel support for graduate students and postdoctoral researchers of any nationality to undertake a collaborative laboratory visit relevant to Development, Journal of Cell Science, or Journal of Experimental Biology. Awards may cover travel, accommodation, and related expenses. Applicants apply through one journal per round.

grants.name: Gerda Henkel Foundation PhD Scholarships
grants.deadlineNote: No fixed deadline; applications may be submitted at any time and committees decide four times a year. Processing takes up to six months.
grants.amount: EUR 1,920 per month for up to two years, plus family allowance
grants.description: Doctoral scholarships in the historical humanities, including history of science, prehistory, early history, archaeology, art history, and legal history. Relevant for history-of-science PhD candidates pursuing dissertation research.

grants.name: Cognitive Science Research Initiative (CSRI)
grants.funder: Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: DST invites project proposals and postdoctoral fellowship applications once a year by advertisement; the most recent call found closed 15 June 2024. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: Project grants covering equipment, manpower, and consumables; 2-year post-doctoral fellowships
grants.duration: Up to 3 years for projects; 2 years for PDF
grants.description: Supports interdisciplinary research in cognitive science, including cognitive neuroscience, computational intelligence, language and cognition, and cognitive disorders. Open to academic and research institutions. Post-doctoral fellow eligibility below age 40.

grants.name: Technology Development Fund (TDF)
grants.funder: DRDO, Ministry of Defence, Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling. RFPs issued through the year on the TDF portal, each with its own submission window.
grants.amount: Grant-in-aid up to 90% of project cost, capped at INR 50 crore
grants.description: Funds Indian MSMEs and startups (with academic partners permitted) to develop defence and dual-use technologies from TRL 3 onwards. Priorities include import substitution and futuristic defence technology under the Make in India framework.

grants.name: Partnership for Accelerating Clinical trials and Entrepreneurship (PACE), SBIRI, and BIPP under BIRAC i4
grants.funder: Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC), Department of Biotechnology
grants.deadlineNote: Periodic joint calls under BIRAC's i4 framework; check the portal for current cycles.
grants.amount: Varies by scheme; PACE academia-industry projects typically INR 1 to 2 crore
grants.description: PACE funds academia developing biotech products of societal value with an industrial validation partner. SBIRI and BIPP support small business and industry-led biotech innovation. Applicants apply jointly through the BIRAC portal.

grants.name: Social Innovation Programme for Products: Affordable and Relevant to Societal Health (SPARSH)
grants.funder: Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC), Department of Biotechnology
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling. SIIP fellowship and SPARSH Category A grants advertised on the BIRAC portal.
grants.amount: Up to INR 50 lakh (Category A); SIIP fellowship INR 50,000/month plus INR 5 lakh kick-start
grants.description: Funds affordable healthcare product development targeting societal health problems. Includes the Social Innovation Immersion Programme (SIIP) fellowship for individuals identifying community health gaps and developing biotech solutions.

grants.name: WISE Fellowship for PhD (WISE-KIRAN)
grants.funder: DST WISE-KIRAN Division, Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: Check the funder's site for the next call. Related tracks include WISE-PDF (post-doctoral), WISE-SCOPE (societal-challenges re-entry), and WIDUSHI (senior).
grants.amount: JRF-equivalent stipend plus contingency
grants.description: Supports women aged 27 to 45 pursuing PhDs in basic and applied sciences at Indian institutions. Part of the WISE-KIRAN umbrella that also runs post-doctoral, re-entry, and senior tracks.

grants.name: DBT Junior Research Fellowship via Biotechnology Eligibility Test (BET)
grants.funder: Department of Biotechnology (DBT) / Regional Centre for Biotechnology
grants.deadlineNote: Annual exam. BET 2026 is closed. Check the funder's site for the BET 2027 announcement.
grants.amount: INR 37,000/month (Cat-I first two years), INR 42,000/month as SRF, plus contingency
grants.duration: Up to 5 years (2 as JRF, 3 as SRF)
