grants.description: National fellowship for PhD research in biotechnology and life sciences at recognised Indian institutions. Category-I holders may join any institution; Category-II are placed at DBT-approved departments.

grants.name: CSIR-UGC NET Junior Research Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: Biannual (June and December cycles) via the NTA CSIR-UGC NET portal.
grants.amount: INR 37,000/month (JRF, 2 years) rising to INR 42,000/month (SRF), plus INR 20,000/year contingency
grants.description: Fellowships awarded on the basis of the CSIR-UGC NET exam for PhD study in chemical, life, mathematical, earth, and physical sciences (and engineering) at CSIR labs, universities, and IITs across India.

grants.name: INSPIRE Fellowship for PhD
grants.funder: Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call; the 2026 portal window ran 24 April to 23 May 2026. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: JRF-equivalent stipend plus research contingency
grants.description: Direct PhD fellowship (no entrance exam) for first-rank postgraduates in basic and applied sciences with minimum 70% marks, or for INSPIRE Scholars. Age limit 22 to 27 years at application.

grants.name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT, Phase II
grants.funder: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: Admissions are run by individual partner institutes, each with its own call and deadline. Check partner institute notices for open calls.
grants.amount: INR 38,750/month (yrs 1-2), INR 43,750/month (yrs 3-5), plus 8% HRA and INR 1.2 lakh/year contingency
grants.duration: Up to 5 years (PhD); PDF and Young Faculty Research Fellowships also supported
grants.description: Supports 1,000 full-time and 150 part-time PhD candidates plus 225 post-doctoral and 50 young-faculty fellowships in ESDM and IT/ITES emerging areas including AI, cybersecurity, quantum, VLSI, and HPC through 2030.

grants.name: Prime Minister's Research Fellowship (PMRF), Direct and Lateral Entry
grants.funder: Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: Selection runs twice a year (May and December cycles), and the call may come later than those months. Applications go through institute nomination; check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: INR 70,000 to 80,000/month plus INR 2 lakh/year research grant
grants.description: PhD fellowship at IITs, IISc, IISERs, NITs, and select institutions in science and technology. Direct entry from top UG programmes; Lateral entry for early PhD scholars. Distinct from the ANRF-CII PMRF-DR industry-partnered doctoral scheme.

grants.name: Bhaskara Advanced Solar Energy (BASE) Fellowship
grants.funder: Indo-US Science and Technology Forum (IUSSTF) / DST
grants.deadlineNote: The page shows no open call. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: Monthly stipend, international return airfare, and contingency allowance
grants.description: Supports Indian PhD students (up to 32 years) and Indian PhD-holders (up to 40 years) working in solar energy for research stints at US institutions. A parallel US track brings US researchers to India.

grants.name: Indo-US Fellowship for Women in STEMM (WISTEMM)
grants.funder: Indo-US Science and Technology Forum (IUSSTF) / DST
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call. Separate Women Overseas Fellowship and Women Student Internship tracks; check the IUSSTF portal for the current cycle.
grants.amount: Monthly stipend, international airfare, and contingency
grants.description: Sends Indian women scientists and engineers to collaborate at US institutions. Student Internship track for PhD candidates aged 21 to 35; Fellowship track for PhD-holders aged 27 to 45 holding a regular academic or R&D position in India.

grants.name: Fund for Improvement of S&T Infrastructure (FIST)
grants.funder: Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: Calls are posted on DST's call for proposals page and the onlinedst portal; the most recent FIST call found there was FIST 2024, which closed 30 April 2024. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: INR 1.5 crore (Level 0) to INR 10 crore (Level 3)
grants.description: Departmental infrastructure grants for science, medical, agriculture, and engineering departments (with 3+ years of PG research) in UGC/AICTE-recognised universities and higher educational institutions. Supports equipment, lab modernisation, computational facilities, and networking.

grants.name: Outstanding Postdoctoral Program
grants.deadlineNote: Annual 15 November deadline for the following academic year.
grants.amount: Tax-free Excellence Fellowship of USD 55,000 per year for three years (paid in NIS)
grants.description: Weizmann fellowship for international postdocs (including CS and mathematics) within four years of their PhD. Open to Indian nationals with a PhD from a non-Weizmann institution. The host lab at Weizmann must be identified before submission.

grants.name: IAS School of Mathematics Membership
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for 2027-28 membership close 1 December 2026 via MathJobs; recommendation letters are due the same day.
grants.amount: Stipend plus housing subsidy; visitor tier available without stipend
grants.duration: One term to a full academic year
grants.description: Open membership for mathematicians and theoretical computer scientists at any career stage; particularly relevant for logic, foundations, and theoretical CS given the annual thematic year. India-based researchers regularly hold memberships.

grants.name: Fields Research Fellowship
grants.funder: Fields Institute for Research in Mathematical Sciences, Toronto
grants.deadlineNote: Annual deadlines 15 January, 15 May and 15 September; submit at least three months before the proposed start. FY27 funding is fully committed, so applications are now for visits starting on or after 1 April 2027.
grants.amount: Living-expense allowance of up to CAD 4,000 per month of full-time residence
grants.description: Short research visit for faculty and research scientists in mathematical sciences, either in residence at Fields or with a collaborator at a Fields Principal Sponsoring University. India-based mathematicians, logicians, and theoretical CS researchers can apply directly with a cover letter, CV, and short proposal.

grants.name: AI for Math Fund
grants.funder: Renaissance Philanthropy (with XTX Markets and others)
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026 round closed for abstracts on 30 March 2026, with decisions in August 2026. Seed grants of up to USD 100,000 are reviewed on a rolling basis.
grants.amount: USD 100K to 1M per project; seed grants up to USD 100K
grants.description: USD 31.5M fund supporting projects that apply AI and machine learning to mathematics, including autoformalisation, theorem proving, and mathematical discovery. Open to individuals and teams worldwide including India-based researchers, students, and postdocs. Strong fit for logic, CS, and math researchers.

grants.name: KAUST Global Fellowship Program
grants.funder: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST), Saudi Arabia
grants.deadlineNote: Call 2027 Stage 1 concept notes closed 1 October 2026. Invited applicants submit full proposals between 15 November 2026 and 15 January 2027.
grants.amount: Full salary plus benefits and an independent research budget
grants.description: Postdoctoral fellowship for early-career researchers to pursue independent research at KAUST, with strong CS, AI, and mathematics divisions. Open to applicants from any country including India.

grants.name: Friedrich Wilhelm Bessel Research Award
grants.deadlineNote: Nominations accepted year-round. Approximately 20 awards per year, with a six-month review.
grants.amount: EUR 60,000 award money
grants.duration: Research stay of up to 12 months in Germany
grants.description: Mid-career award for internationally recognised researchers up to 18 years post-PhD, to spend up to a year with German collaborators. Nomination-based via a German host academic; India-based CS and logic researchers with strong research profiles are directly eligible.

grants.name: DFG Mercator Fellowship (Mercator Module)
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling. The Mercator Fellows module is requested within a DFG project proposal, so it follows that programme's deadlines.
grants.amount: Covers travel and residence during German stays plus a lump sum
grants.duration: Flexible; several visits over the project lifetime
grants.description: Enables India-based researchers to join a DFG-funded German project as a long-term collaborator through extended research stays in Germany, awarded via a German PI's proposal. Broadly applicable to CS and logic collaborations with German groups.

grants.name: Toyota Foundation International Grant Program
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026 call ran from 1 April to 30 May 2026. The 2027 call has not been announced.
grants.region: Asia (India eligible; project must span 2 or more Asian countries)
grants.amount: Up to JPY 10,000,000 (approx USD 65,000) for two-year projects; JPY 5,000,000 for one-year
grants.description: Grants for cross-border Asian collaboration on shared societal issues, including science policy, technology in society, and computational approaches to public problems. India is on the eligible-country list (with Bangladesh, Bhutan, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka); projects must be led jointly across at least two eligible countries.

grants.name: DRDO DIA-CoE Research Problems September 2026
grants.funder: Directorate of Futuristic Technology Management (DFTM), DRDO, Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: Notice valid through December 2026 for 19 specified research problems. Proposals routed to the relevant DIA-CoE research vertical. No fixed award ceiling or duration stated.
grants.amount: See call details
grants.description: Multi-institutional, multidisciplinary research proposals addressing 19 defence research problems through the DRDO Industry Academia-Centre of Excellence (DIA-CoE) network. Topics include stealth materials, aerospace modelling, radar and signal processing, autonomous navigation, power electronics, semiconductor detectors, and fuzing. Open to Indian academia and national research institutes using the official proposal forms.

grants.name: TNQ Inspiring Science Awards (ISA) 2027
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 31 October 2026. Eligible papers must have been first published between 1 October 2025 and 30 September 2026, with the applicant as first or co-first author.
grants.amount: Apple laptop, medal, and citation for eight finalists; winner also receives a conference travel fellowship
grants.description: Annual award recognising the best full-length life-sciences research paper by a student from India. Open to PhD researchers and postdoctoral fellows within four years of their postdoctoral programme, where the work was conducted at an India-based institution.

grants.name: ASM Future Leaders Mentorship Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for the 2027 cohort open in February 2027 and are due in March 2027. Exact date not announced.
grants.amount: Structured mentoring, leadership and professional-development training, networking and collaboration opportunities
grants.description: Two-year online programme pairing master's and doctoral students in microbial sciences with experienced mentors across academia, industry, government, and other sectors. Fellows must be ASM members for 2027, hold master's or doctoral student status, show a strong microbial-sciences background, and commit to the full two-year term.

grants.name: DHR Human Resource Development Sub-Scheme for Health Research 2026-27
grants.funder: Department of Health Research (DHR), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: Proposals due via DHR e-PMS portal by 5:00 PM on 30 November 2026. Current call restricted to applicants from Northeastern states: Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura.
grants.amount: See call details
grants.description: Capacity-building programme for advanced medical and health research. Covers the Women Scientist Fellowship Programme and the NRI/PIO/OCI Research Support Programme under the HRD Sub-Scheme. 2026-27 call limited to applicants from the eight Northeastern states.

grants.name: MCQST Junior Researcher START Fellowship
grants.funder: Munich Center for Quantum Science and Technology (MCQST)
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026 call closed at 23:59 CEST on 24 October 2026; reference letters were due 31 October 2026. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: Up to EUR 300,000 (salary, staff, equipment, consumables, travel)
grants.description: Independent-project fellowship for outstanding early-career researchers in quantum science and technology. Applicants must secure an MCQST PI host who provides infrastructure and a support letter.

grants.name: Syngene Early Career Research Grants 2026-27
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 30 November 2026. Three grants awarded. PhD in science and no more than eight years post-PhD as of December 2026. Permanent institutional position required; postdoctoral researchers not eligible. Institution must hold a CSR Registration Number.
grants.amount: INR 50 lakh per grant (excludes institutional overheads); three grantees
grants.description: Early-career research grants for innovative work spanning biology, chemistry, computation, and technology relevant to drug discovery and healthcare. Open to permanently appointed junior faculty, assistant professors, and junior research faculty in life sciences at Indian research institutes or universities.

grants.name: Pfizer Real World Evidence on Early Appropriate Use of Aztreonam-Avibactam (ATM-AVI)
grants.deadlineNote: Proposals due 23:59 EST on 25 November 2026. Projects expected to run June 2027 to December 2028. Applications must come from organisations, not individuals. Indian organisations require a valid FCRA certificate and IRB/IEC approval before project start.
grants.amount: Up to USD 50,000 per project; 2 to 3 awards; indirect costs capped at 28%
grants.description: Real-world clinical studies evaluating the impact of early, appropriate aztreonam-avibactam use guided by rapid diagnostics in adults with suspected or documented CRE or Stenotrophomonas maltophilia infection. PI must be an employee or contractor with an MD, PhD, equivalent research doctorate, advanced nursing, pharmacy, or microbiology degree.

grants.name: World Cancer Research Fund Regular Grant Programme 2026-27
grants.deadlineNote: Letter of intent call open 5 October to 13 November 2026, 5pm UK time. Outcomes in February 2027; final decisions end of September 2027. Open to researchers anywhere in the world.
grants.amount: Investigator-initiated grants up to GBP 500,000; pilot and feasibility grants up to GBP 60,000
grants.duration: Up to 4 years (investigator-initiated); up to 2 years (pilot/feasibility)
grants.description: Research on diet, nutrition, body composition, physical activity, and sleep in cancer prevention or survivorship. Eligible organisations may be located anywhere in the world.

grants.name: ICMR First in the World Challenge Grants 2026
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 5:30 PM on 30 November 2026 via e-PMS. Open to scientists at Indian government medical colleges, INIs, ICMR institutes, universities, recognised R&D laboratories, NGOs (with required registrations), start-ups, MSMEs, and industry. At least one co-PI from the PI's institution is mandatory.
grants.amount: Up to INR 1 crore (proof of concept), 4 crore (prototype), or 8 crore (final product or implementation model)
grants.duration: Up to 2, 3, or 4 years by stage
grants.description: Supports high-risk, high-reward biomedical and health-technology ideas that have not previously been thought of, tested, or tried anywhere. Three stages: proof of concept, prototype development, final product or implementation model. Applicants may apply individually or in teams.

grants.name: UNESCO-Al Fozan International Prize for Young Scientists in STEM
grants.deadlineNote: Nominations close midnight (UTC+1) on 30 November 2026. Eligible institutional nomination required; self-nominations are not accepted.
grants.amount: Prize for recognition of scientific contribution (see nomination page for current prize value)
grants.description: Biennial UNESCO prize recognising five young scientists under 40 for outstanding contributions in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM). Candidates must be nominated by an eligible institution, government, or professional body.

grants.name: MathWorks Call for Research Proposals
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 2 November 2026 at 11:59 PM EST. Applicant must be the PI and include a letter of intent from a commercial partner.
grants.amount: Up to USD 20,000 unrestricted gift
grants.description: One-year research gifts for industry-relevant projects that use MATLAB or Simulink and advance AI-enabled engineering. Priority areas include aerospace and UAV systems, automotive and electric vehicles, wireless and radar, energy, robotics and autonomous systems, medical devices, and semiconductors. Open to current full-time faculty at accredited doctoral institutions.

grants.name: FCDO SRHR Applied Research Centre
grants.deadlineNote: Expressions of interest close 30 November 2026, 17:00 GMT. The centre runs July 2027 to March 2032 and must be led by an eligible LMIC institution, with the core programme covering at least six LMICs.
grants.amount: Up to GBP 12 million
grants.description: Establish an applied research centre addressing evidence gaps in sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR). The centre will conduct demand-led research, strengthen capacity, and support evidence use across at least six low- and middle-income countries. A single LMIC institution or LMIC-led consortium may apply.

grants.name: DBT Emerging Frontiers in Biotechnology (EFB) 2026
grants.funder: Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: Ashoka's research office lists a 15 November 2026 deadline; DBT's own programme page describes submission windows of 1 January to 31 March and 1 July to 30 September through eProMIS. Confirm on DBT's site before applying. Industries and start-ups are not eligible.
grants.amount: Up to INR 100 lakh per project
grants.description: Investigator-led competitive research grants under two verticals: Biomedical Sciences (human health and disease, vaccines, diagnostics, drug development, genomics, biosensors) and Biological Sciences (plant, agricultural, and animal biotech, bio-energy, bio-resources, environmental biology). Open to researchers at academic institutions and R&D organisations.

grants.name: CSIR Travel Grant Scheme
grants.funder: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research - Human Resource Development Group (CSIR-HRDG)
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling. Applications must arrive 2 to 4 months before the event. No CSIR travel assistance in the prior three years.
grants.amount: Up to full actual airfare from the nearest Indian airport to the event and back
grants.description: Travel support for young Indian researchers, research associates, resident doctors, emeritus scientists, and other non-regular researchers presenting at international scientific events. Applicants need relevant qualifications, refereed publications, an accepted lead- or single-author paper or invited chair/keynote role, and institutional endorsement.

grants.name: Qualcomm Innovation Fellowship India
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026 India round closed 20 April 2026. The 2027 India call has not been announced.
grants.amount: INR 10 lakh per winning team per year, renewable once
grants.description: Fellowship for PhD and master's teams at 16 eligible Indian institutes including IISc, IITs, IIITs, and ISI Kolkata, with a Qualcomm research mentor. Covers CS, AI, systems, and signal processing. Requires a short research proposal and faculty endorsement.

grants.name: Simons-Berkeley Research Fellowship
grants.funder: Simons Institute for the Theory of Computing, UC Berkeley
grants.deadlineNote: The Fall 2027 call (Diffusion Generative Modeling programme) opened 1 October 2026; applications are due 1 December 2026.
grants.amount: Competitive stipend, housing, and visa support
grants.description: Semester-long fellowship for theoretical computer scientists and mathematicians within five years of their PhD. Fellows participate in a Simons Institute programme on topics such as pseudorandomness, high-dimensional expanders, or symmetry in computation. India-based postdocs are eligible subject to home-institution approval.

grants.name: Dagstuhl Seminar Proposals
grants.funder: Schloss Dagstuhl, Leibniz Center for Informatics
grants.deadlineNote: Two windows per year, closing 15 April and 1 November, submitted through DOSA. Hybrid proposals are allowed only when the current round's call says so.
grants.amount: Full travel and accommodation for invited participants
grants.duration: 5-day on-site seminar for up to 48 participants
grants.description: Teams of three to four computer scientists from different institutions can propose a week-long seminar at Dagstuhl, Germany, around a well-defined research theme. India-based researchers can serve as organisers and name invited participants, with Dagstuhl paying local costs for all invitees. Hybrid proposals require a separate concept section addressing time-zone and remote participation issues.

grants.name: Oberwolfach Workshop Proposals
grants.deadlineNote: Annual 31 July deadline for workshops two years later. The next window closes 31 July 2027 for 2029 workshops.
grants.amount: Full lodging and meals at MFO for all participants
grants.description: Mathematicians can propose a full, half-size, or mini-workshop at the Oberwolfach institute. Proposals need a scientific focus, suggested participant list, and organiser team; female participation and representation are strongly encouraged. India-based mathematicians can lead or co-lead proposals. Distinct from the Research in Pairs (OWRF) scheme.

grants.name: Mitacs Globalink Research Internship
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call; the call for Summer 2027 internships has closed. Mitacs says the call is usually open for about six weeks and posts the deadline when it opens.
grants.amount: Round-trip airfare, housing, and student fees covered
grants.description: Research internship at a Canadian university for Indian BE and BTech students in their third or fourth year, matched to a Canadian faculty host. Students apply to three to ten projects across three or more provinces, with a minimum 70% cumulative GPA. The India track funded through AICTE supports about 300 interns per year.

grants.name: Infosys Prize
grants.deadlineNote: Annual prize; nominations are by invitation and generally open early in the year for about three months. The funder publishes each year's dates a few weeks in advance.
grants.amount: USD 100,000 purse plus medal and citation
grants.description: Annual prize for researchers of Indian origin working anywhere, or any researcher whose work impacts India, aged 40 or under. The Mathematical Sciences category explicitly covers mathematics, statistics, and theoretical computer science. Nominations come from senior researchers, not the candidate; the prize covers six categories including Physical Sciences and Engineering.

grants.name: SNSF Scientific Exchanges (as invited guest)
grants.deadlineNote: Proposals can be submitted at any time through mySNF, at least four months before the event or visit. Each applicant may apply once per calendar year.
grants.amount: Travel, accommodation and meals for visitors; research visits of 1 to 6 months, at CHF 3,500/month for visitors from DAC-list countries
grants.duration: Up to 6 months for a research visit, up to 5 days for an event
grants.description: An India-based researcher cannot apply directly, but Swiss hosts can bring them in as a visiting guest for up to six months or as a speaker at a workshop. Both the host and the visitor must hold a PhD for research visits; PhD students are eligible for event invitations. Useful for India-Switzerland collaborations with an existing Swiss counterpart.

grants.name: Simons Pivot Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026 round is under review. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: Full academic-year salary plus USD 10,000 research allowance; follow-on award up to USD 1.5M
grants.duration: 1-year training year, with a 5-year follow-on grant for selected fellows
grants.description: Supports faculty with a PhD or MD who want to pivot into a new field in natural sciences, engineering, mathematics, data science, or computer science. The fellow spends a year training with a mentor in the target field; the mentor receives USD 50,000. Open to faculty at institutions worldwide including India, subject to the home institution granting a full year of leave.

grants.name: Isaac Newton Institute Programme Proposals
grants.funder: Isaac Newton Institute for Mathematical Sciences, Cambridge
grants.deadlineNote: Two deadlines per year, 31 January and 31 July, for programmes running two to three years later.
grants.amount: Participant travel and subsistence at INI during the programme
grants.description: Mathematicians and theoretical computer scientists can propose a thematic research programme at INI in Cambridge, co-organised with other senior researchers. Proposals cover mathematical sciences and cross-disciplinary mathematics, including statistics, data science, and mathematical biology. India-based researchers can co-organise and visit INI during the programme, which usually hosts around 50 visiting fellows.

grants.name: Global EbA Fund Medium-size Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 16 November 2026. Projects must qualify as ecosystem-based adaptation, build on existing work, partner with local institutions, and target global, thematic, or ODA-eligible contexts. Government entities may collaborate but cannot receive grant funds.
grants.amount: Up to USD 500,000 per grant
grants.description: Collaborative, innovative projects that scale ecosystem-based adaptation through enabling environments, finance, human security, and policy alignment. Open to universities, research institutes, legally recognised NGOs, INGOs, IGOs, community-based and Indigenous Peoples' organisations, eligible private-sector companies, and consortia.

grants.name: Laura Bassi Scholarship (Winter 2026)
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 15 November 2026. Awards editorial assistance (not cash). Open worldwide without institutional, departmental, or national restrictions.
grants.amount: Editorial assistance valued at USD 750 (master's), USD 2,500 (doctoral), USD 500 (junior academics), or USD 5,000 toward open-access charges for eligible book authors and editors
grants.description: Funds editorial assistance for research on neglected topics in any discipline. Open to currently enrolled master's and doctoral candidates, and to academics within five years of starting full-time employment. The separate Bassi Foundation Press award supports eligible book authors and editors through an open-access publication charge.

grants.name: DBT Translational Biotechnology Research Networks
grants.funder: Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling advertisement open from 7 September 2026 to 7 September 2027. Submit a Letter of Intent of up to 500 words through eProMIS.
grants.amount: See call details
grants.description: Concise, high-impact biotechnology ideas that either bridge discovery and application through a clear translation pathway, proof of concept, and scale-up potential, or pursue discovery-driven frontier science with transformative potential. Scope includes health and life sciences; agriculture, food, and bioresources; environment, climate, and sustainability; industrial biotechnology; synthetic biology, genomics, engineering biology, and computational biology.

grants.name: Jawaharlal Nehru Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling. Applications accepted on a continuing basis. One fellowship awarded annually.
grants.amount: INR 1,00,000 per month plus up to INR 75,000/year for secretarial assistance, travel, and contingencies
grants.description: Two years of freedom to pursue original and creative work. Open to Indian citizens across sciences, humanities, and public life, including scholars in any discipline, writers, journalists, artists, and civil servants.

grants.name: BBSRC Bioinformatics and Biological Resources Fund (26BBR)
grants.funder: Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council (BBSRC), UK Research and Innovation
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 19 November 2026. Project lead must be at a UK research organisation eligible for BBSRC funding. India-based researchers may participate as international project partners only.
grants.amount: Up to GBP 2 million full economic cost; BBSRC funds 80% up to GBP 1.6 million
grants.description: Supports community bioinformatics or biological resources serving UK bioscience, including databases, software, and biological materials. Useful route for Indian collaborators partnering with UK PIs.

grants.name: NQS Mission 2: Components, Systems, and Architectures
grants.funder: EPSRC and STFC, UK Research and Innovation
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 24 November 2026. Latest start date 31 May 2027. An eligible UK research organisation must lead. India-based researchers may participate as international project partners only.
grants.amount: Up to GBP 2.56 million full economic cost; EPSRC funds 80%
grants.description: Research on quantum-networking components, systems, and architectures, including nodes, routers, memories, repeaters, photonics, integration, security, and distributed capability. Part of the UK National Quantum Strategy. Useful route for Indian quantum groups partnering with UK PIs.

grants.name: UKRI Enabling AI Adoption across Science and Engineering
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 1 December 2026, 4:00pm UK time. Fixed start date 26 April 2027; an eligible UK research organisation must lead, and Indian researchers may join as project partners.
grants.amount: Up to GBP 250,000 full economic cost; UKRI funds 80%
grants.description: Exploratory collaborations between AI specialists and domain researchers addressing important scientific and engineering challenges. Useful route for Indian AI or domain-science groups partnering with UK PIs.

grants.name: IBSA Foundation Fellowships 2026
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 31 January 2027. Applicants must be under 40 on that date. Permanent professors are ineligible.
grants.amount: EUR 32,000 per fellowship (seven fellowships)
grants.description: Seven early-career biomedical fellowships across dermatology, endocrinology, fertility and urology, orthopaedics and pain medicine, and healthy ageing. Open to applicants of any nationality holding a degree in medicine, biology, pharmacy, biotechnology, or bioengineering. Eligible categories: PhD students, PhD holders, postdoctoral researchers, and medical residents.

grants.name: AssisTech Foundation Student Innovation Challenge: collaborATe 2026
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 30 October 2026. Listed on the Manthan-Utthan platform (sign-in required to view).
grants.amount: See call details
grants.description: Student innovation challenge for assistive technologies addressing accessibility and disability. Open to student teams developing hardware, software, or systems that improve quality of life for persons with disabilities.

grants.name: Temasek Foundation Green Future Innovation Challenge
grants.deadlineNote: Submissions close 4 February 2027; the Grand Finale is in Beijing in April 2027.
grants.amount: See call details
grants.description: Challenge for green and sustainable innovation addressing climate, environmental, and ecological problems. Open to applicants worldwide. Delivered in partnership with regional institutions.

grants.name: The Liveability Challenge
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 12 February 2027.
grants.amount: Over SGD 5.5 million in grants, investment and development opportunities across the edition; SGD 1 million grant for the top Oceans solution
grants.description: Global search for solutions addressing urban liveability challenges including energy, food, water, decarbonisation, and the built environment. Finalists receive funding and support to deploy their solutions in Singapore and beyond.

grants.name: CAMPCO Development of All-Season Cocoa Varieties for the Belt
grants.funder: The Central Arecanut and Cocoa Marketing and Processing Co-operative Ltd (CAMPCO)
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 6 November 2026. Listed on the Manthan-Utthan platform (sign-in required to view).
grants.amount: See call details
grants.description: Agricultural research call for developing suitable all-season cocoa varieties for the Indian cocoa belt. Open to researchers at Indian institutions working in plant breeding, crop science, and agricultural biotechnology.

grants.name: Rohini Nilekani Centre for Brain and Mind Seed Grants
grants.funder: Rohini Nilekani Centre for Brain and Mind, NCBS and NIMHANS
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 1 December 2026. Applicants must be faculty at a research institute or university with DSIR certification, with at least 5 years of service remaining to superannuation.
grants.amount: Up to INR 25 lakh
grants.description: Supports research into the biological basis of mental illness and improving diagnosis and clinical management. Open across disciplines as long as the proposal aligns with RN-CBM objectives. Prior experience in stem cells or neuroscience is not required; RN-CBM supports skills and training acquisition during the project.

grants.name: ANRS MIE Emergences PRFI 2026
grants.funder: ANRS Emerging Infectious Diseases (ANRS MIE), France
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 7 January 2027 at 23:59 Paris time. Projects must be co-led by a team in France and a team in a low- or lower-middle-income country; India qualifies as lower-middle-income.
grants.amount: See call details
grants.description: Collaborative research on emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases, especially viral haemorrhagic fevers, respiratory viruses, and arboviruses. Projects may span basic, translational, clinical, public-health, or humanities and social-science approaches.

grants.name: Sonar Research Grant Program
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling. Applications accepted while quantities remain available.
grants.amount: In-kind access to SonarQube commercial licences (Cloud Enterprise and Advanced Security). Programme commitment totals USD 2.8M; per-award value not stated.
grants.description: In-kind SonarQube access for academic software-engineering research. Priority topics include code quality and developer productivity, technical debt, and AI-enabled remediation. Open to accredited universities and research institutions, including research leaders, professors, postdoctoral researchers, PhD candidates, and graduate researchers.
